text-theme-text-sec mt-v6/12 text-pretty">Investigate recurring production errors from Datadog, identify root causes, and propose fixes</p><div class="mt-v1 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-g0.5"><a href="https://cursor.com/automations/new?templateId=investigate-datadog-errors" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="btn">Try Automation<span class="ml-1">↗</span></a></div></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>Production errors surface in Datadog faster than anyone can chase them down. An agent can investigate the moment an error spikes, trace it to the responsible code, and propose a fix while the context is fresh.</p><h2 id="what-it-does">How to investigate Datadog production errors with Cursor</h2><ul><li><strong>Watches.</strong> <!-- -->Fires when a production error is reported in Datadog, via the Datadog trigger or a webhook.</li><li><strong>Investigates.</strong> <!-- -->Pulls the error, traces, and logs from Datadog, inspects the repository, and opens a pull request or comment.</li><li><strong>Reports back.</strong> <!-- -->A root-cause summary linked to the offending code, escalating to a fix PR when the change is contained.</li></ul><h2 id="prerequisites">Prerequisites &amp; integrations</h2><p>Connect these in your<!-- --> <a href="https://cursor.com/dashboard/integrations" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Cursor integrations settings</a> <!-- -->before you enable the automation:</p><ul><li><a href="https://cursor.com/dashboard/integrations" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Datadog</a></li></ul><p>Trigger<!-- -->:<!-- --> <!-- -->Webhook</p><h2 id="the-prompt">The prompt</h2><p>This is the prompt that ships with the template on the<!-- --> <a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/automations/investigate-datadog-errors" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Marketplace</a>. Open the template in Automations to load it, then adapt it to your team.</p><div class="group relative my-v2"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy prompt" class="border-theme-border-01 bg-theme-card-02-hex hover:bg-theme-card-03-hex text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text absolute top-2 right-2 z-10 flex cursor-pointer items-center gap-1 rounded-xs border p-1.5 opacity-0 transition-opacity duration-150 group-hover:opacity-100 focus-visible:opacity-100"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="8" y="8" width="14" height="14" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button><pre class="my-0! max-h-[24rem] overflow-y-auto whitespace-pre-wrap"><code>You are an incident-investigation automation focused on Datadog errors.

## Goal

Continuously reduce production errors by investigating high-impact Datadog signals and landing safe fixes.

## Investigation process

1. Use Datadog tools to identify top errors by frequency, user impact, and recency.
2. Group duplicate symptoms into root-cause clusters.
3. Correlate stack traces, service metadata, deployment timing, and relevant code changes.
4. Form a root-cause hypothesis and validate with code evidence.

## Fix policy

- Only implement fixes with high confidence in root cause.
- Prefer minimal, robust changes with low regression risk.
- Add tests where feasible for the failure mode.
- If a safe fix is not possible, provide a concrete follow-up plan.

## Output

If fixed, open a PR and report:
- Error signature(s) addressed
- Root cause
- Fix summary and validation
- Any remaining risk</code></pre></div><h2 id="how-to-set-up">How to set up automatic production error investigation</h2><ol><li><a href="https://cursor.com/automations/new?templateId=investigate-datadog-errors" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Open the template in Automations</a> <!-- -->to start from it.</li><li>Connect the repository the agent should work in.</li><li>Choose the trigger and connect the tools it uses —<!-- --> <!-- -->Datadog, Webhook<!-- -->.</li><li>Tune the prompt to your quality bar, then activate the automation.</li></ol><h2 id="tips">Tips for customizing error investigation for your services</h2><ul><li><strong>Tighten the quality bar.</strong> Tell the agent to comment with its findings instead of opening a pull request when it is not confident, so humans stay in the loop on risky changes.</li><li><strong>Send updates where the team works.</strong> Add a Slack channel so results land in the flow of work instead of waiting to be noticed.</li><li><strong>Start narrow, then widen.</strong> Scope the trigger to one repository, branch, or label first, and expand once you trust the results.</li><li><strong>Make it Team Owned.</strong> Set billing to a team-owned automation so runs are shared and visible across the team.</li></ul></div></div></div><div class="col-span-full class="prose prose--block"><p>Production errors surface in Datadog faster than anyone can chase them down. An agent can investigate the moment an error spikes, trace it to the responsible code, and propose a fix while the context is fresh.</p><h2 id="what-it-does">How to investigate Datadog production errors with Cursor</h2><ul><li><strong>Watches.</strong> <!-- -->Fires when a production error is reported in Datadog, via the Datadog trigger or a webhook.</li><li><strong>Investigates.</strong> <!-- -->Pulls the error, traces, and logs from Datadog, inspects the repository, and opens a pull request or comment.</li><li><strong>Reports back.</strong> <!-- -->A root-cause summary linked to the offending code, escalating to a fix PR when the change is contained.</li></ul><h2 id="prerequisites">Prerequisites &amp; integrations</h2><p>Connect these in your<!-- --> <a href="https://cursor.com/dashboard/integrations" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Cursor integrations settings</a> <!-- -->before you enable the automation:</p><ul><li><a href="https://cursor.com/dashboard/integrations" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Datadog</a></li></ul><p>Trigger<!-- -->:<!-- --> <!-- -->Webhook</p><h2 id="the-prompt">The prompt</h2><p>This is the prompt that ships with the template on the<!-- --> <a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/automations/investigate-datadog-errors" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Marketplace</a>. Open the template in Automations to load it, then adapt it to your team.</p><div class="group relative my-v2"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy prompt" class="border-theme-border-01 bg-theme-card-02-hex hover:bg-theme-card-03-hex text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text absolute top-2 right-2 z-10 flex cursor-pointer items-center gap-1 rounded-xs border p-1.5 opacity-0 transition-opacity duration-150 group-hover:opacity-100 focus-visible:opacity-100"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="8" y="8" width="14" height="14" rx="2" ry="2"></rect><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"></path></svg></button><pre class="my-0! max-h-[24rem] overflow-y-auto whitespace-pre-wrap"><code>You are an incident-investigation automation focused on Datadog errors.

## Goal

Continuously reduce production errors by investigating high-impact Datadog signals and landing safe fixes.

## Investigation process

1. Use Datadog tools to identify top errors by frequency, user impact, and recency.
2. Group duplicate symptoms into root-cause clusters.
3. Correlate stack traces, service metadata, deployment timing, and relevant code changes.
4. Form a root-cause hypothesis and validate with code evidence.

## Fix policy

- Only implement fixes with high confidence in root cause.
- Prefer minimal, robust changes with low regression risk.
- Add tests where feasible for the failure mode.
- If a safe fix is not possible, provide a concrete follow-up plan.

## Output

If fixed, open a PR and report:
- Error signature(s) addressed
- Root cause
- Fix summary and validation
- Any remaining risk</code></pre></div><h2 id="how-to-set-up">How to set up automatic production error investigation</h2><ol><li><a the repository the agent should work in.</li><li>Choose the trigger and connect the tools it uses —<!-- --> <!-- -->Datadog, Webhook<!-- -->.</li><li>Tune the prompt to your quality bar, then activate the automation.</li></ol><h2 id="tips">Tips for customizing error investigation for your services</h2><ul><li><strong>Tighten the quality bar.</strong> Tell the agent to comment with its findings instead of opening a pull request when it is not confident, so humans stay in the loop on risky changes.</li><li><strong>Send updates where the team works.</strong> Add a Slack channel so results land in the flow of work instead of waiting to be noticed.</li><li><strong>Start narrow, then widen.</strong> Scope the trigger to one repository, branch, or label first, and expand once you trust the results.</li><li><strong>Make it Team Owned.</strong> Set billing to a team-owned automation so runs are shared and visible across the team.</li></ul></div></div></div><div class="col-span-full
